data.narrative:
Ampaire, a Series A–stage aerospace company founded by Kevin Noertker and Cory Combs, has raised $74M to date. The Space & Aerospace sector includes 6 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers at various stages, though a narrow peer set of same-stage or valuation-tier matches is insufficient for reliable median-based triangulation.

Of three valuation methods tested, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($74M) as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier from Series A to subsequent stage, this method implies a valuation of $148M. Peer-median anchoring was rejected due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds (n≥3). Public-comp anchoring could not be executed because Ampaire's revenue is not disclosed; while the Space & Aerospace sector median trades at 27.4x P/S, revenue opacity prevents application.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $126M (low) to $170M (high), centered on $148M. This range is narrow and rests on a single method, making it sensitive to assumptions about stage-step multipliers and the appropriateness of using total raised as a valuation proxy. Key uncertainties include Ampaire's actual revenue trajectory, capital efficiency relative to public peers, and near-term funding environment. Wider conviction would require either disclosed revenue or access to a denser set of private-market transaction data in aerospace.
